blocker.summary: r469 (pure log re-analysis of r465's already-captured 573s run, no new process launched) found two concrete facts via the already-instrumented ac6_world_submission_owner_probe.cpp diagnostic (active in every run since r465 via --mission-render-summary): the world-manager tick function (rex_sub_8226CEA0) is called ZERO times across the entire 573s run, and the async DATA00.PAC read stream stops at 95.2% (2,158,782,464 / 2,267,086,848 bytes) after ~3 minutes of active streaming, never resuming. Critically, the game keeps rendering actively after the PAC stream stops (frame counter already past 15000, real draw counts 128-149/frame, continuous GPU presents) -- this is NOT a freeze, which further weakens the 'movie worker stuck' theory (r466/r467) and strengthens a new lead: the game is likely stuck on a confirmation screen (hangar/map/sortie) with its own render loop, never advanced because the automated route never sends the needed input. run_gate.py already has named flags for exactly this (--mission-hangar-confirm, --mission-map-confirm, --mission-sortie-long-press, etc.), never tried in combination with --mission-render-summary by this chain. Named for r470: try those confirmation flags in one bounded live run; if that fails, re-read an existing screenshot from r465-r468 to identify the stuck screen directly. native profile untouched this cycle (no rebuild). Still open, non-blocking: reconsider the PinnedShaderRuntime backlog commit (r433/r434/r438/r454-r468) independently if the campaign/world ceiling proves too costly to lift.
